blocks.content: PART A: BACKGROUND OF ECONOMIC REFORMS IN INDIA

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Economic Reforms of 1991 were launched to address a severe Balance of Payments crisis and foreign exchange depletion.
Liberalisation aimed to end the rigid 'License-Permit Raj' and reduce regulatory control over private enterprise.
Privatisation entailed selling government stake in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to improve corporate efficiency.
Globalisation integrated India's domestic economy with the world market by lowering tariffs and inviting FDI.

blocks.content: 1. Indian Economy Before 1991

Before 1991, India followed a planned, controlled and regulated economic system. The economy was characterised by licence raj, excessive government control, dominance of public sector, import substitution, high trade barriers and low competition.
Growth rate was low, productivity was poor and Indian industries lacked global competitiveness.
2. Economic Crisis of 1991
By 1991, India faced a severe balance of payments crisis. Foreign exchange reserves fell to critically low levels, sufficient to finance only a few weeks of imports.
Major causes included rising fiscal deficit, mounting external debt, high inflation, inefficiency of public sector and global economic shocks.
PART B: MEANING OF ECONOMIC REFORMS
3. Economic Reforms
Economic reforms refer to changes in economic policies aimed at improving efficiency, productivity, growth and global integration of the economy.
PART C: LIBERALISATION
4. Meaning of Liberalisation
Liberalisation refers to the removal or reduction of government controls and restrictions to allow free functioning of market forces.
5. Features of Liberalisation
CHAPTER 15: LIBERALISATION, PRIVATISATION & GLOBALISATION (LPG REFORMS)

• Abolition of licence raj

• Reduction of industrial licensing

• Freedom to expand production

• Reduction in price controls

• Simplification of procedures
6. Objectives of Liberalisation
To increase efficiency, encourage competition, attract investment and promote economic growth.
PART D: PRIVATISATION
7. Meaning of Privatisation
Privatisation refers to the transfer of ownership, management or control from the public sector to the private sector.
8. Forms of Privatisation

• Disinvestment

• Outsourcing

• Public-private partnership

rows: Removal of state-imposed restrictions, quotas, and licensing rules
To foster market freedom and economic deregulation
Transfer of government ownership or management to private hands
To enhance enterprise efficiency and reduce fiscal burden
Integration of domestic economy with foreign economies
To encourage free trade, foreign investment, and global mobility

blocks.content: 9. Objectives of Privatisation
To improve efficiency, reduce fiscal burden, encourage competition and enhance productivity.
PART E: GLOBALISATION
10. Meaning of Globalisation
Globalisation refers to the integration of a country’s economy with the global economy through free flow of goods, services, capital, technology and labour.
11. Features of Globalisation

• Reduction of trade barriers

• Foreign direct investment

• Entry of multinational corporations

• Technological transfer
PART F: IMPACT OF LPG REFORMS
12. Positive Impact
Higher growth rate, increased foreign investment, improved efficiency, technological advancement and global integration.

items: SSC exams frequently ask for the year of implementation of the New Economic Policy (1991) and the Prime Minister/Finance Minister duo at that time (P.V. Narasimha Rao and Dr. Manmohan Singh).
Understand the key difference between Disinvestment and Strategic Sale in Privatisation.
Be prepared for questions on foreign direct investment (FDI) limits and deregulation of industrial licensing.

blocks.content: 13. Negative Impact
Income inequality, unemployment in some sectors, environmental degradation and vulnerability to global shocks.
PART G: LPG REFORMS AND SSC EXAM RELEVANCE
14. SSC Exam Perspective
SSC frequently asks questions on definitions, objectives, features and impacts of liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation.
SSC EXTREME FINAL REVISION POINTS

• LPG reforms began in 1991

• Liberalisation reduces controls

• Privatisation transfers ownership

• Globalisation integrates economy globally
